compute.note: Parameters: 64 from the method string (high confidence); the circuit code builds 64 one-parameter gates (SU2_symmetrized._get_dimerizarion_layers: range(1) x 4 shifts x (8 + 8) pairs), which reproduces it. Iterations: 2000 = 1000 natural-gradient steps without symmetry projection, then 1000 continuing with the 128-element projector (n_iter default 1000; main.py is called twice and passes only lr). As published, Optimizer.optimize() ends with "return res.x" on the circuit object, which has no attribute x, so the first call exits with an AttributeError and "&&" would skip the symmetric run; the step counts are therefore what the code intends, not what it can be shown to have run, hence confidence low. Samples: none; the method string says exact gradients on a state vector. The code has no exact branch that main.py reaches: it draws binomial estimates with the default 2^36 shots (--log2samples default 36), which is exact to about 4e-6 relative. Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 5d1ebf9 (2022-11-11, Nikita Astrakhantsev); the program was added to methods in 6887677 (2024-08-10) ("wip: added the VQE simulator"; next commit "VQE simulator: dusted-off version runs"), so it is a later reconstruction. The VarBench SM (arXiv:2302.04919 Sec. S3 D) describes the ansatz and the natural-gradient update but no step count. No device or time is recorded. || pass 2026-09-27: circuit_schedule restored from route 1b's pass (merge.mjs copied only the BLOCK fields and dropped it), plus dimension = C(16, 8) = 12870: the S^z = 0 sector without lattice symmetry the state vector lives in (the calibration runs measured the step time at exactly this D). runs keep the intended 1000 + 1000 steps; as published the first call ends in the res.x AttributeError and && skips the symmetric run, so 1000 steps actually execute (verify/agent-A.md item 6, DOUBTFUL x2; no change).
